# Eski Lua runtime

The C runtime embeds Lua5.1.5 and helper modules from Valkey8.1.0 at commit67c8683792fc9ab7e295f833478eca180c5e4691. Only deps/lua source and the repository licence were acquired. manifest.json records every upstream file URL and original SHA256. LICENSE.lua, LICENSE.valkey and the source files retain upstream legal notices. Local changes to upstream files are recorded in patches/valkey-module-allocation.patch, patches/lua-unpack-range.patch and patches/lua-line-count-error.patch. The range patch validates unpack result counts before reserving stack space and prevents signed index overflow. The official Lua5.1.5 archive and checksum are retained for provenance comparison. The runtime/ directory and ABI bindings are original Eski implementation.

include/eslua.h is the ABI, mirrored by include/eslua_ffi.odin and src/lua_runtime/ffi.odin. C owns all Lua API allocation and protected longjmp boundaries. Odin callbacks never invoke Lua API. Result output belongs to the caller until eslua_free_result. A host command or ACL reply remains borrowed until the next command/ACL callback or invocation completion. Log and busy callbacks do not release that reply.

eslua_eval executes in a persistent thread-local VM and eslua_compile syntax-checks text in a fresh protected VM without running it. eslua_reset releases the EVAL engine, and eslua_eval_stats reports its retained allocation. SCRIPT FLUSH and shutdown own the reset boundary. Binary chunks are rejected. EVAL globals and builtins are readonly; user table metatables and raw access are supported. Standard5.1 string/table/math, os.clock, cjson2.1, cmsgpack0.4, struct and BitOp1.0.2 are exposed. cjson.new returns an independent configurable object. Runtime-owned codec allocations are bounded and tracked; private CJSON working buffers are reclaimed per call while encode_keep_buffer retains its public configuration value. This changes internal buffer reuse without changing encoded values.

eslua_library_load stages a library in one persistent shared Functions VM, permits both registration signatures and retains per-library callback registry references, a shared readonly load environment and per-library upvalues. Loading has a registration-only environment; callbacks resolve the full runtime environment. Registration outside load remains forbidden even through a captured registration table. Library load fails atomically from the caller's perspective; the host owns publication, collisions between libraries, persistence and retirement. Library metadata bytes remain borrowed until library_free. Every call resets invocation callbacks, arguments, script RESP, abort state and metrics while preserving the VM and upvalues. library_stats reports its engine-wide allocation. functions_stats aggregates active and retired Functions engines once. functions_reset detaches the current engine while existing library handles keep a retired engine alive; its memory is reclaimed after the last handle is freed. Deleting the final library preserves module configuration, while FUNCTION FLUSH resets it. FUNCTION RESTORE FLUSH preserves module configuration. Functions loads have a cooperative timeout; C work runs between hooks.

Callbacks append acl_check and propagation after opaque. ACL returns a RESP integer1/0 or error frame without executing commands. Propagation uses NONE0/AOF1/REPLICA2/ALL3. Options append an identifier and function_mode to provide uncaught-error script context. Returned error tables remain separate from uncaught errors. The Odin host owns actual ACL/read-only/flags admission, cache, effects propagation, atomicity and BUSY service.

Memory/output/instruction/depth controls are requested-allocation bounds rather than process RSS or a preemptive wallclock deadline. Default limits and exact command compatibility are still being qualified. Persistent-library failures retain earlier successful dataset effects. Output allocations are detached from VM allocation ownership before return, so results can outlive a library handle. VM close and all CJSON configuration finalizers run in C with the correct allocation owner. A protected preallocated cleanup closure unregisters library callback references without relaxing the configured memory limit.

This runtime does not by itself establish full server Lua compatibility. Exact error wording, full command admission, Functions persistence and a real interactive debugger require integration and conformance evidence. Reply serialization uses explicit heap frames, preserving partial nested arrays and a terminal Lua stack-limit error for cycles without recursing on the C stack. Debug helpers currently return without an active debugger; SCRIPT DEBUG sessions are a host integration boundary.

Options.debug_mode selects disabled, forked YES or synchronous debugging. Appended debug_read/debug_write callbacks exchange complete RESP command/log frames. C owns all inspection, eval and hook operations; the host owns transport and process isolation. The debugger queues command traces with line stops, implements stepping/breakpoints/source/locals/upvalues/eval/trace/maxlen, and sends an endsession array before returning the ordinary invocation result. Abort retains synchronous effects; disconnect aborts forked execution and resumes synchronous execution. Continuing an infinite Lua loop returns a timeout prompt. Debugger eval reuses the readonly/text-only sandbox. Its extra nonterminal timeout is enabled only with an explicit instruction budget; default debugger evaluation has no additional deadline, matching the reference.

Nested debugger evaluation uses the pinned Lua5.1 state's allowhook and savedpc fields. The active frame's saved PC is synchronized before nested Lua calls, and the original hook permission is restored before returning from the outer hook. This allows bounded inspection evaluation while preserving valid stack/error source lookup. All such work stays under the existing protected C invocation. Debugger request/log/format/breakpoint allocations use tracked transient ownership and are reclaimed at invocation completion.

The math.random stream is shared by EVAL and Functions on the coordinator thread. Explicit math.randomseed changes that shared stream; neither SCRIPT FLUSH nor FUNCTION FLUSH resets it. The two engines retain separate default cjson configuration, while all libraries in the Functions engine share its actual module userdata. Explicit cjson.new instances remain independent.

Uncaught error messages and compile errors retain their bytes up to the configured output/memory budgets. Oversized output produces an explicit limit error rather than silent truncation. Status/error text truncates at NUL; uncaught exceptions receive script context after truncation. error_reply removes one leading error marker and supplies ERR when the remaining text contains no ASCII space. Returned err/ok numeric fields remain ordinary table data, while thrown numeric err fields are converted as reference errors.

The exposed Lua5.1 surface includes string.dump, the REPL_SLAVE alias, and the EVAL-only internal error descriptor helper. Dumped bytecode is never accepted by the VM loader. The descriptor helper returns or updates caller-owned error tables using raw fields and reports only the caller source/line; it exposes no host pointers or debugger libraries. Helper error wrappers preserve the original Lua call-site prefix and function name. Compiler errors use the reference command wrapper, and uncaught loaded chunks retain their actual source name.

Functions libraries reuse one immutable registration environment per engine. Its global lookup exposes only registration metadata while loading and resolves the full runtime globals during callbacks, including captured registration tables. Reusing this environment avoids retaining multiple equivalent Lua tables for every library. The optional immutable lua-enable-deprecated-api configuration adds getfenv, setfenv and newproxy to the VM bootstrap; the default keeps them absent. Options.enable_deprecated_api carries that decision across the protected C boundary.

RESP3 command attributes are consumed without exposing metadata to Lua, and attributed errors retain their host error origin. Big-number reply text follows the reference line sanitization policy for both client protocol versions. Command error tables expose the reference ignore_error_stats_update boolean field; Result.forwarded_error carries that exact boolean through returned or uncaught errors so the host can mark command failure without counting a forwarded error twice. Other field types do not suppress accounting.

Each serialized error frame also carries an owned Result.errors descriptor containing its byte offset, message length and exact ignore flag. Nested arrays therefore update each error prefix once while forwarded command errors avoid duplicate counts. Descriptors are allocated under the same protected memory budget as output, detached with it and released by free_result; failed serialization drops partial descriptors. detached_memory reports the actual outstanding result-buffer and descriptor allocation sizes, including allocation headers, independently of VM retention. Results and descriptors remain valid after their originating VM or library is closed.
